newsitem.title: USA: Tentative pact reached by union, Wheeling-Pittsburgh.
newsitem.headline: Tentative pact reached by union, Wheeling-Pittsburgh.

text.p: Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Corp. and the United Steelworkers of America said Friday they reached a tentative agreement to end a 10-month-old strike, the longest in the nation's steel industry.
The tentative pact, whose terms were not disclosed, will be submitted to the local union presidents for their action and to the members for ratification, the company and union said in a statement.

About 4,500 steelworkers at Wheeling-Pittsburgh have been on strike since Oct. 1, 1996, making the dispute the longest ever in the U.S. steel industry. The strike has idled eight steel plants in Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio.

The strike has centred around the issue of pensions. The union has demanded that the company establish a plan that would guarantee that a certain amount of money be contributed to a worker's plan each month.
The company, a unit of WHX Corp., has said it cannot afford such a plan.
